titel: The value of your earning capacity
kurz: The present value of your future earned income is the largest item on your personal balance sheet, yet it appears on no portfolio statement.

bloecke.md:
Most statements of wealth start with the securities account and stop at the current account, so the largest item is missing. People in work in their early thirties own an asset that far exceeds all others: the claim to their own future earned income. In financial economics it is called [[human capital]]. It is not held at any bank and can be neither sold nor borrowed against. It can, however, be valued using present value, the same method that is used to value bonds and companies.

For comparison, the net worth of a typical German household in 2023 was around €103,000 (median according to the Bundesbank's wealth survey; because of very wealthy households, the mean according to the income and consumption survey (Einkommens- und Verbrauchsstichprobe) is €230,400). The present value of an average working life is many times higher, yet hardly anyone keeps track of it.

bloecke.erklaerung: Present value of an income stream that grows by g each year and is discounted at r. It is the same formula as for a growing annuity, except that the series of payments here consists of earned income.
variablen: present value of human capital today
net income in the first year
discount rate, that is, the price for the income arriving only later and without certainty

bloecke.titel: From gross salary to present value
bloecke.md:
The median full-time salary in 2025 was €54,066 gross a year. For a childless person with no church affiliation in tax class I (Steuerklasse I), this leaves around €34,500 net, or just under €2,880 a month. This is our own calculation, based on the 2026 tax scale under Section 32a EStG (Income Tax Act), an employee's share of social security contributions of 21.75% and the average additional health insurance contribution (Zusatzbeitrag).

At 32, there are still 35 years of work left until 67. If pay rises by 2% a year in nominal terms and is discounted at 4%, the formula gives a present value of around €851,000. Without discounting, the net incomes add up to about €1.7 million. A medium-sized portfolio hardly matters by comparison.

bloecke.titel: Human capital and financial assets over a working life
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation for a career start at 25 with €30,000 net, 2% income growth, discounting at 4%, a 15% savings rate and a 5% investment return. Financial assets only exceed human capital at just under 58.

serien.name: Human capital (present value of future net income)

bloecke.md:
## How human capital develops

Human capital is a stock that is used up over the course of a working life. With every year worked, part of it turns into money, that is, into consumption or financial assets. At first the present value still grows, even though in the model incomes grow more slowly than the rate at which they are discounted. With each year, all future incomes move one year closer and are discounted less heavily. As long as many working years lie ahead, this increase is larger than the income of the year just ended, which drops out of the calculation. After that, the present value shrinks at an accelerating pace because fewer and fewer years remain. In the model above, the maximum is reached around the age of 31, and at 67 the value is zero by definition.

Measures that increase human capital therefore have the greatest effect early in a working life, and measures concerning the portfolio only later. Twenty hours spent selecting funds at 28 improve the smaller of the two quantities.

The discount rate expresses your own income risk. A permanent salary in the public sector is a bond-like stream of payments and justifies a low rate. Commission income in a cyclical industry should be discounted at a higher rate. The table shows how strongly the rate affects the present value.

bloecke.titel: Present value of 35 years of net income (starting at €34,500), in thousands of euros

bloecke.md:
## Salary negotiation as a return decision

A pay rise permanently lifts the entire future income stream. Its effect is multiplicative, because all later percentage increases build on the new level. Employees who know the median salary and the range in their industry can argue with their market value instead of their need. This is the only part of the negotiation that can be prepared.

On an income of around €54,000, €1,000 more gross pay leaves around €525 net, by our own calculation. The rest goes on social security contributions and income tax. Why the share deducted first rises with increasing salary and then falls again above the contribution assessment ceilings is explained in the lesson on gross pay, net pay and the marginal tax rate. For the present value calculation, the result is enough. Projected over 35 years and discounted, this €525 is worth around €12,900 today.

bloecke.titel: Present value of a pay rise and of a higher return
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation, all values as present value today over 35 years. With a small portfolio, a pay rise achieves much more than a higher return; with six-figure portfolios, the values converge.
kategorien: +1 point of return on a €20,000 portfolio
+1 point of return on a €100,000 portfolio

bloecke.md: In the first fifteen years of a career, the salary lever is almost always the bigger one, because the portfolio is still small and the income stream still long. Later the relationship reverses. Attention should therefore go first to salary and later to the portfolio.

## Further training as an investment

A qualification costs money and time and in return brings a permanently higher income. In structure, this is the same calculation as for a machine in a company. In both cases, the state shares in the acquisition costs through the tax system, although for the machine this is spread over the years of depreciation. Work-related further training costs, by contrast, are [[income-related expenses (Werbungskosten)]] in full and usually reduce taxable income as early as the year of payment. The tax saving depends on the marginal tax rate, not the average tax rate. An exception is your first vocational training. Its costs only count as special expenses (Sonderausgaben) and only up to €6,000 a year, which usually brings no tax saving in years of training without significant income.

bloecke.titel: Payback of a qualification gained alongside work
bloecke.md:
The qualification costs €12,000 and is work-related. With taxable income of around €42,000, deducting it as income-related expenses reduces income tax by around €3,600 (our own calculation under Section 32a EStG 2026). The after-tax cost is therefore about €8,400.

If the qualification permanently raises gross salary by 6%, from €54,066 to just over €57,300, around €1,690 a year of this remains net. The costs have therefore paid for themselves after just under five years; without the tax effect it would take just over seven years.

The time invested is not included in this calculation. If 500 hours are spent, they should be valued at what they would otherwise have been worth. This time is the main part of the price and the reason why further training without a clear prospect of higher income rarely pays off.

## Taxation of side income

Income from a second job is added to the rest of your income and is therefore taxed at the top end of your income, that is, at the marginal tax rate. With a salary of €54,000, roughly €2,700 of a €4,000 fee from a side activity remains after income tax. The negotiated hourly rate therefore paints too favourable a picture.

There are three exceptions you should know. A mini-job (Minijob) of up to €603 a month (as of 2026, linked to the minimum wage of €13.90) remains free of tax and social security contributions for the employee alongside a main job subject to social insurance. Only for pension insurance is there a contribution, and you can apply to be exempted from it. The employer usually pays a flat-rate tax on the mini-job. A second mini-job, by contrast, is added to the main job. The trainer's allowance (Übungsleiterpauschale) under Section 3 no. 26 EStG makes certain part-time secondary activities tax-free up to €3,300 a year. Side income below €410 a year remains effectively untaxed thanks to hardship relief (Härteausgleich).

In comparison, twenty hours of preparation for a salary negotiation often yield a higher expected hourly wage than twenty hours of a side job. They also do not eat into recovery time that would then be missing in the main job.

## Benefits beyond gross salary

Gross salary is only the visible part of what a job offers. A comparison of jobs that looks only at this figure overlooks items that together can easily make up a fifth.

bloecke.md:
For this job, the employer pays around €65,500 a year, and around €34,500 arrives in the account. The difference of around €31,000 is made up of just over €23,000 in social security contributions from employer and employee and around €7,800 in income tax. It explains why a negotiated rise has to be large for noticeably more money to arrive net.

## Lack of diversification in human capital

Nobody would call a portfolio consisting of a single share sensible. Yet human capital is similarly concentrated, because it depends on one employer, one industry, one qualification, one country and one currency. This concentration cannot be avoided. What can be avoided is doubling it in your financial assets.

Doubling occurs when financial assets carry the same risks as income, for example with shares in your own employer, sector funds for your own field of work or a property located where the only large employer in the region is based. In a downturn, salary, portfolio and property value then fall at the same time, precisely when liquidity is needed. A well-known example is the collapse of Enron in 2001. Employees lost their jobs and their retirement savings in the same week, because both depended on the same company.

bloecke.unter: The axes determine how large the emergency fund needs to be and which investments in the portfolio would double the income risk.
bloecke.yLabel: co-movement with the stock market (high at the top)

felder.text: Mechanical engineering, cars, construction, chemicals. Salary flows steadily until the economy turns. Short-time work (Kurzarbeit) and dismissal then come when the market is down as well.
Sales, finance, tech. Income and portfolio fluctuate in step. Largest emergency fund, smallest position in the employer's shares.
The payment stream behaves like a bond. It is crisis-proof and thus takes pressure off the low-risk part of your wealth.
Trades, medical practices, creative professions. Income fluctuates, but independently of the stock market. The problem is liquidity.

bloecke.md:
Employee shares almost always come with a discount or a tax allowance, and this advantage is real. The problem only starts with holding the shares. Employees who tie their salary and retirement provision to the same company carry a [[cluster risk]] that cannot be offset even with many other holdings in the portfolio.

Experience shows that the information advantage employees believe they have is smaller than the loyalty they feel. Trading on inside information is prohibited anyway. Written investment policy statements often record the question of whether you would buy this share today at this price if you did not work there. It serves as a touchstone and is not a recommendation.

A present value of €851,000 assumes that the ability to work is preserved. About one in four people becomes occupationally disabled at least once during their working life. The main cause is mental illness (32.3% of cases according to MORGEN & MORGEN 2026); accidents account for only around 7%.

The statutory reduced earning capacity pension (Erwerbsminderungsrente) is no substitute. For full reduced earning capacity it averaged €1,059 a month in 2023. It requires a remaining capacity of less than three hours a day in any occupation at all, and over 40% of applications are rejected. The lesson on insurance covers how this asset can be insured. For this lesson it is enough to recognise that this is about protecting the largest item on your personal balance sheet and not about a minor add-on policy.

mitnehmen: Until well into your fifties, human capital is the largest item on your personal balance sheet. In the model, its present value peaks as early as around the age of 31.
A permanent pay rise affects the entire future income stream. In your early thirties, 5% more gross pay corresponds to around €35,000 of present value.
Work-related training costs reduce taxable income, and the tax saving depends on the marginal tax rate. This shortens the payback period by years.
Side income is taxed at the marginal tax rate. Less of the agreed gross hourly rate therefore remains than the figure in the contract suggests.
Shares in your own employer concentrate income risk and portfolio risk on the same company.

begriffe.text: The present value of all a person's future earned income. For most people in work under 50, human capital is their largest asset. It can be neither traded nor borrowed against, but it can be valued and insured.

The unit of calculation for the statutory pension. One year of work at average earnings (provisionally €51,944 in 2026) gives 1.0 point. Since 1 July 2026, one point has been worth €42.52 of gross pension a month.

Expenses incurred to earn, secure and maintain income, for example for work-related further training. They reduce taxable income, so the tax saving depends on the marginal tax rate. Without proof, a flat €1,230 is deducted.
An accumulation of several risks from the same source, for example when your job, a portfolio position and the location of your property depend on the same company or the same industry.

A payment by the employer into a savings contract, often governed by a collective agreement and made only on request. If taxable income is low, the state adds up to €122.30 a year as an employee savings allowance (Arbeitnehmersparzulage).
